name: pygments-recoverable-extendedregexlexer-8288
instr:
Pygments cannot suspend ExtendedRegexLexer tokenization at a yielded-token boundary and safely resume it in another process. Implement portable checkpoints for direct lexer, public library, and command-line use without changing behavior when checkpoints are unused. Failures yield no tokens and never partially replace an existing destination. Preserve preprocessing, token streams, filtering, highlighting return values, stream ownership, encodings, and command-line output without checkpointing.

Capture only state affecting future tokens, including distinct callback and context state for BibTeX, Terraform, Crystal, Haxe, Sass, YAML, Snowball, and Clean. Use deterministic JSON that round-trips without executable Python objects. Resume with the exact indexed suffix and absolute offsets matching original source slices. Before recovery reaches tokens, callbacks, or filters, validate lexer class, tokenization options, source identity, schema, and checkpoint semantics. Isolate mutable state for every recovery. Checkpoints remain reusable after complete, partial, failed, or abandoned recovery; an end-of-input checkpoint yields nothing. `resume_lex` accepts checkpoint objects or serialized text, removes offsets, and applies configured filters exactly once in their existing order. Malformed or truncated data raises `CheckpointError`, incompatibility raises `CheckpointMismatch`, and future versions raise `UnsupportedCheckpointVersion`.

Terraform heredoc checkpoints survive encoding. Dec
